scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Qhapaq negro originated in the Cusco Region of Peru as an Andean expression of devotion that references historical Afro-Peruvian identity.
The name combines the Quechua word 'qhapaq' (meaning noble, principal, or mighty) with Spanish 'negro', invoking sub-Saharan African ancestry within a traditional sacred performance.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The Qhapaq negro is staged during Marian feast days, including celebrations honoring Our Lady of Mount Carmel (Mamacha Carmen) and the Festival of the Virgin of the Rosary.
It expresses religious veneration, community identity, and local historical memory.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Variants exist across different towns within the Cusco Region, including performances in Paucartambo and Huallhua in Calca Province.
The Qhapaq negro is categorized as an indigenous American folk dance tradition of Peru, performed in festival contexts alongside related Andean dances such as Ch'unchu, Qhapaq Qulla, and Saqra.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Qhapaq negro is sibling of Ch'unchu: Performs alongside Qhapaq negro in traditional Cusco regional Marian festivals.
Qhapaq negro is sibling of Qhapaq Qulla: Performs in the same festival context and shares linguistic naming structure ('qhapaq').
Qhapaq negro is sibling of Saqra: Appears during the same Cusco regional feast day celebrations.
